record.original_question: Is the second-order gravitational Poisson equation independently valid as the gravitational field equation inside sources and on large distance scales, or is it only a sufficient way to obtain the observed Newtonian exterior potential? The problem is to determine whether observations or a principle uniquely require the second-order Poisson equation, rather than an alternative such as a fourth-order Poisson equation that also yields the Newtonian potential as a dominant short-distance exterior solution.

evidence.quote: While Eq. (10) was chosen so as to yield Eq. (11), it is a curious but not well appreciated fact that there is actually not yet any evidence for the independent validity of Eq. (11) in the interior of a gravitational source - in the exterior region alone one can only test the validity of the (Newtonian) solution in that region, this not being sufficient to infer the validity of the Poisson equation itself in that and all other regions as well.
However, interior to atoms Eq. (14) has never been tested, simply because gravity is not the predominant force there.

Thus as of today the dynamical consequences of the second order gravitational Poisson equation which go beyond those of Newton’s Law have yet to be tested, thus making it unnecessary to find a covariant generalization of the second order Poisson equation; rather one only needs to recover its exterior solution in some limit.
We thus see that while a second order Poisson equation is sufficient to yield Newton’s Law of Gravity, it is not in fact necessary, with a fourth order Poisson equation being just as capable.

Thus the case for the unique use of the second order Poisson equation (and acordingly of its second order Einstein generalization) on large distance scales has yet to be made; and of course, should such a case eventually actually be made, then after all that, dark matter would still have to be found.

artifact.self_contained_problem: In Newtonian gravity, the gravitational potential φ produced by a mass density ρ is conventionally taken to satisfy the second-order Poisson equation ∇²φ = 4πG ρ. Outside an isolated, spherically symmetric source of total mass M this yields the Newtonian exterior potential φ(r) = −GM/r. However, alternative local field equations can produce the same exterior Newtonian potential. For example, the fourth-order Poisson equation ∇²(∇²φ) = g(ρ) (for a suitable source term g(ρ)) admits, outside the source, general spherically symmetric solutions of the form φ(r) = −A/r + B + C r + D r², and thus also reproduces −GM/r as the dominant short-distance exterior behavior. Both equations agree with Newton's law in the exterior region of a localized source, but differ in their predictions inside matter and on sufficiently large distance scales.\n\nProblem. Determine whether there exists an empirical observation, a symmetry, or a first principle that uniquely singles out the second-order Poisson equation ∇²φ = 4πG ρ as the gravitational field equation valid both inside sources and on all distance scales, rather than admitting an alternative such as the fourth-order Poisson equation that yields the same Newtonian exterior potential as a dominant short-distance solution. Equivalently: produce either (i) a test, observation, or principle that excludes all higher-order linear local alternatives whose exterior solutions contain the −GM/r term, or (ii) a concrete consistent alternative theory (with field equation different from the second-order Poisson equation) that agrees with all current gravitational observations.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is conceptual: no observation has tested the second-order Poisson equation strictly inside matter, and higher-derivative Poisson-type equations (which arise e.g. in conformal gravity and other fourth-order gravity theories) remain viable in producing the Newtonian exterior potential. The proponent of conformal/fourth-order Newtonian gravity (Mannheim and collaborators) continued to pursue this alternative, and no decisive observation or principle uniquely selecting the standard second-order Poisson equation has been established. The question therefore remains open.

status_evidence.title: Making the Case for Conformal Gravity
status_evidence.snippet: Mannheim argues that fourth-order conformal gravity provides an alternative to standard second-order gravity that reproduces Newtonian behavior in suitable limits while differing on galactic and cosmological scales.
status_evidence.claim: A fourth-order gravitational equation remains a viable alternative whose Newtonian limit reproduces −GM/r exterior behavior, indicating that the second-order Poisson equation is not uniquely required by current observations.

status_evidence.title: Alternative to Dark Matter and Dark Energy
status_evidence.snippet: Conformal gravity yields a fourth-order Poisson equation whose static spherically symmetric solution contains a Newtonian -GM/r term plus additional linear and quadratic terms in r, fitting galactic rotation curves without dark matter.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-order gravitational field equations consistent with the observed Newtonian exterior potential continue to be actively studied, supporting the open status of the necessity question.
